component.name: Sugo
component.summary: Pomodoro timer with configurable presets and session statistics

description.p: Sugo is a Pomodoro timer for Linux desktops, at home on KDE Plasma, and for macOS. It provides configurable work and break phases, timer presets, session history, and productivity statistics.
Sugo is an independent project and is not an official KDE application.

ul.li: Work, short-break, and long-break phases with configurable durations and cycle count
User-defined presets with categories, symbolic icons, notification controls, and automatic-start modes
Configurable phase-end sounds, one-minute pre-alarm, and optional ambient focus audio
Optional screen-sleep inhibition during work phases
Session history, streak tracking, and charts
SQLite backup, restore, and session-history management
System tray integration and a D-Bus control interface
Optional calendar events for finished work sessions (Nextcloud login or any CalDAV calendar)
KRunner integration, optional automatic pause when the screen is locked, and task notes for completed sessions

description.p: Sugo can send anonymous usage statistics (the version, the kind of system, which features are on, the planned length of each phase and whether it was finished) to help improve it. They are off unless you turn them on, in the welcome tour or in the settings, and never include personal data.
More time when a phase needs it, a session that survives a restart, signed updates, and many fixes.

ul.li: Add 2, 5 or 10 minutes to a phase, even right after it ends, from the Focus page, the tray, the notification or the command line
A session under way when Sugo quits or crashes comes back, paused, at the next start
A suggestion for the break appears under the clock
The tray icon turns yellow while the timer is paused, and Quiet in the composer shows clearly whether it is on
Statistics list every session of the period, and a session can be deleted together with its calendar event
Several timers can be chosen and deleted at once on the Timers page, also from the keyboard
Sugo warns before quitting would lose data not saved yet, and says when the stored timers could not be read or the calendar password is not in the keyring
AppImage and Flatpak for Linux on ARM (aarch64), and updates are signed and checked before they are installed
Sugo Sync: a new device gets the key only after you confirm the code it shows, and a lost answer no longer breaks a token renewal or a new recovery code
Fixes to calendar sync, the screen lock, KRunner, backups, notification silencing and the macOS menu bar

description.p: Anonymous usage statistics, which you choose to share or not, and a round of fixes.

ul.li: Usage statistics are off until you turn them on, in the welcome tour or in Settings; the documentation lists exactly what is sent
The accent colour reaches the sliders, the timer icons and the running badge in the menu bar, and the cycle bar is taller and easier to grab
The timer editor keeps its title and groups Reset, Revert and Save; dropdown menus open centred on their field
Number fields step from the number you typed, and a sideways scroll no longer steps them
Calendar sync keeps unsent events across a restart and after a note update, and an accepted event lifts the pause
The start command resumes a paused timer, and notifications still show when the server's capabilities can't be read
Waiting for the key in Sugo Sync reads the device list again after a minute

description.p: Sugo has moved to its new home, github.com/sugoHQ/sugo, and its app ID is now stream.sugo.app.

ul.li: Updates are taken from the new address too
Start at login is carried over to the new app ID, except in the Flatpak, where it has to be turned on again
The Flatpak installs as a new app and imports the data and settings of the old one at its first start

description.p: A new look: a title bar with the timer, statistics and settings, and a composer to choose the timer and start it.

ul.li: Choose an accent colour, used by the main buttons, switches, sliders, the cycle track and the running badge in the menu bar
Settings in categories beside the page, with a Timers category listing every timer and an About page
Statistics with today's work time and sessions, the figures in one strip, quieter charts and the task notes of the shown period
The update shows as a small icon in the title bar, and the search has the look of the menus
Calendar sync finds Nextcloud calendars by itself, shows their colours, accepts an address without https:// and handles refused requests better
The screen lock is noticed on GNOME, Xfce, Cinnamon and MATE too, and work that starts by itself waits while the screen is locked
Backups made by Sugo 1.0.0 can be restored, and the 1.0.0 data that 1.0.1 moved aside is taken back
Many fixes to notifications, sounds, the keyring, the tray menu and the macOS app

description.p: Welcome macOS: Sugo now runs on macOS 13 or later, on Apple Silicon and Intel Macs.

ul.li: A native Mac app: menu-bar countdown, Dock badge and menu, app menu and shortcuts, native notifications, Keychain and login item
On macOS, notifications are silenced during work with a Focus through Shortcuts, the timer can be controlled with sugo:// links, and the app updates itself from the release disk image
Export the session history as CSV or JSON, and remove only the sessions older than a few months
Reset the settings to their defaults, show the welcome tour again, and open the database folder from the settings
More focus sounds, with sounds and alerts that fade in and out
Resize the phases of the cycle bar with the mouse, and choose the timer over D-Bus
Diagnostics can record Sugo's debug messages on request
Fixes: our window buttons hide when KWin forces its title bar, and the layout no longer moves when a message comes or goes
Work, short-break and long-break phases with configurable durations, cycle count and automatic-start modes
Timers of your own with categories and icons, starting from a classic Pomodoro that silences notifications while you work
An interface of its own, dark or light, with a command palette, keyboard shortcuts and the window buttons of your desktop
An animated welcome tour
Statistics by day, week, month and year, streaks, and breakdowns by timer, category and task
Task notes for finished work sessions, from the notification or an in-app prompt
Notification silencing and screen-sleep inhibition during work, with optional automatic pause when the screen is locked
Phase-end sounds, a one-minute pre-alarm and optional ambient focus audio
A system tray icon with a live countdown, start at login, KRunner commands and a D-Bus interface
Optional calendar events for finished work sessions (Nextcloud login or any CalDAV calendar)
Local SQLite storage with backup and restore, and a diagnostics report
An AppImage that updates itself, from the stable releases or the nightly builds
